answer: Persistent neighborhood aging. Each agent's reach is scored by the count of distinct counterparties that keep returning across epochs—a rising tide of repeat links, not one-off contacts. New identities start with no history, so their edge weight is near zero until sustained multi-epoch interaction accumulates. An attacker must run many identities through an entire voyage of cycles with genuine recurring partners before gaining routing weight, and each abandoned identity leaves a relic of decayed edges that never transfers. Cost: full multi-epoch participation per identity, non-refundable.
